messages:
sam.partnerships: Quick thread — the supplier (OpenWeightsCo) just dropped a delivery package for ModelX v2. Need legal + eng alignment on what we can actually ship to marketplace / SI partners. Package contains: raw checkpoints in S3, tokenizer files, conversion scripts, and a LICENSE.md that looks restrictive. Questions below.
tara-legal: Saw it. Main red flag: LICENSE.md is 'research-only' with an explicit non-commercial clause. That prevents marketplace commercial listing and Dedicated/resold deployments. Also no export-control/geo restrictions stated — we need confirmation.
nate-eng: If it's research-only we can't hand out weights to customers or include in Dedicated. We could host a restricted hosted API if supplier signs a hosting license. Tokenizer also has custom BPE trained vocab — need license for that too.
anya-ops: Ops note: their S3 layout currently grants cross-account write access to their CI role. We must avoid shared write creds. Request: presigned URLs for upload + a signed manifest (hash list) for each artifact.
ben-partners: I spoke with their PM earlier; they're open to discussing commercial terms but want attribution and IP protection. They mentioned a per-customer addendum as a likely path. I can loop them in.
claudia-ml: Technical: model bundles include a proprietary fused-attention kernel; conversion scripts call a closed-source binary blob. We need either source or a redistributable binary with checksum and install instructions for our runtime. Also ask for a small eval prompt set for quality checks.
sam.partnerships: Tara — what's the minimum license change to allow a Marketplace listing (hosted + marketplace listing but protecting their IP)? Can we accept 'no redistribution of raw checkpoints' and still list?
tara-legal: Short answer: yes, with a tailored grant. Proposed approach: allow commercial use and hosting, prohibit redistribution of raw checkpoints, permit distribution of compiled/quantized runtime artifacts under a redistributable runtime license. Also require supplier to sign a Distribution License Addendum (DLA) and complete an export compliance questionnaire.
nate-eng: That sounds workable. From runtime side we want: manifest with SHA256 checksums, signed provenance file, and a minimal compliance test (smoke inference + accuracy on their eval set). Also request kernel licensing details (source vs binary).
anya-ops: For SI/on‑prem integrations: if they refuse raw weights, we can prepare an 'install kit' (container + runtime + license enforcement). That requires supplier consent for redistributing runtime images to SIs under contract.
ben-partners: I'll propose two lanes to them in the email: 1) Hosted + Marketplace listing (requires commercial permitted license + provenance + DLA for listed artifacts) 2) SI / Dedicated (requires DLA + SOW + KYC for onprem transfer). I'll cc legal and eng and ask for timeline.
sam.partnerships: Tara — can you paste a short template clause we can push to them so I can include it in the email?
tara-legal: Sure, use this as a starter clause: 
```
Grant: Supplier grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, sublicensable license to host, serve, and distribute compiled model artifacts (runtime binaries/quantized weights) to Redwood customers. Redistribution of raw checkpoints is prohibited. Commercial use permitted. Supplier retains all IP rights.
Export Control: Supplier certifies that the model and artifacts are not subject to export restrictions beyond those declared; parties will cooperate on any required licenses.
Provenance: Each release must include a signed manifest (SHA256) and a provenance file with build instructions.
```
Add a KYC/export paragraph for SI transfers.
claudia-ml: Also ask if they'll provide kernel source or a redistributable binary with a versioned checksum and a compatibility doc (FP16/INT8 support, max context length, kv-cache semantics). That avoids runtime surprises.
nate-eng: And include an explicit compatibility matrix: supported sequence length, tokenization norm, memory/per-token perf for typical batch sizes. We'll need that for model profiles in the console.
sam.partnerships: Ben — once you send the draft, post their replies here. We want to lock the DLA + packaging in the next 2 weeks so marketing can plan a joint announcement at the start of next month.
tara-legal: Timeline: if supplier signs the DLA as-is, legal can finalize in ~2 weeks. If they push on clauses, expect 4-6 weeks. Recommend we prepare a small checklist for supplier to fill out immediately: kernel/source, license acceptance, export declarations, intended allowed uses.
ben-partners: Draft going out now, looping their PM and engineering lead. Will report back. :eyes:
deploy-bot: created JIRA PARTNERS-421: "supplier DLA + packaging" — assignee: ben-partners.
